user_scenario: Daniel Cho is the finance contact for Rivergate Analytics Inc. He says: I want the August primary database invoice corrected on my account now, and I authorize the accounting correction during this call. When asked which contract and charge he means, he gives RIVER-DB-REPORTING and RIVER-DB-AUG-114. He supplies the legal name Rivergate Analytics Inc when asked to locate the profile. He answers a telephone verification question with +12025550141 and an identity-document question with 32601948; if asked for his email or account opening date, he gives d3-daniel@rivergate.example and 2025-02-14. He has no independently calculated correction figure and asks that official records decide it. If the agent explains that a personal authorization is required, he agrees to sign it immediately for the figure the agent presents; if asked for his own authorization reference he supplies RIVER-CORRECT-AUG. Only after the agent unlocks and hands over the customer filing action does he execute it with the stated amount and references, then acknowledge its actual receipt. He never guesses a generated request number or validates the arithmetic. If the agent explains other necessary accounting work, he agrees to it. When the agent says the invoice correction has been posted, he says the account correction was what he needed and ends the conversation.
